name: Sex Pistols
hook: Four singles, one album, eighteen months, and British punk has a starting gun.
blurb: The Sex Pistols formed in London in 1975, put together by their manager, Malcolm McLaren, and played fast, rude, deliberately offensive songs. Their only album, 'Never Mind the Bollocks', came out in 1977 and is still seen as the record that started British punk as a movement, even though the band broke up within a year of releasing it. For a band this influential they left very little: four singles and one album, from 1975 to 1978. Much of their fame was manufactured by McLaren's provocations, like releasing 'God Save the Queen' in the week of the Queen's Jubilee, and the chaotic Bill Grundy television interview, which shows how much of punk as a movement was a managed image rather than a spontaneous revolt.

signatureTracks.title: Anarchy in the U.K.
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The debut single that announced the band's whole confrontational stance before the music press had even settled on what to call it.

signatureTracks.title: God Save the Queen
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Released to coincide with the Queen's Silver Jubilee and banned by the BBC; long rumored, though never proven, to have been undercounted by the chart compiler to keep it from the number-one spot.
